messages.subject: NaNs produced in pcount output
parts:
Hi All,

Thanks in advance for any help.

I have counts of animals on three consecutive nights, at four time points throughout the year (summer, autumn, winter, spring), across seven years. However, my aim is purely to predict abundance at each combination of site*season*year and so I have chosen to use pcount() instead of pcountOpen() as I have no interest in modelling gamma or omega.

I can create my data frame with no problems, but when I run and then summarise my desired model I get warning: In sqrt(diag(vcov(obj))) : NaNs produced, and have NANs in my model output. There are several good posts on this group that describe similar problems (here and here), but these have not yet helped me to solve my error. 

Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Please see data attached and code below. 

# Load data
pcnt <- read.csv("pcount_dat.csv", header = TRUE)

# Define y and siteCovs  
y <- pcnt[,2:4]
siteCovs <- pcnt[,6:9]
  
# Create UMF
umf <- unmarkedFramePCount(y = y, siteCovs = siteCovs)
summary(umf)

# Run model
m2 <- pcount(~site ~site + year + season + offset(log(dist)), data = umf, K = 574, mixture = "NB", se = TRUE)
summary(m2)


# Once I am confident my model works appropriately, I plan to predict from this model as follows
new_dat <- siteCovs
new_dat$dist <- 1

pred <- predict(m2, type = "state", newdata = new_dat)
pred$abun <- exp(pred$Predicted)

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] NaNs produced in pcount output
parts: A quick fix is to subtract 2000 from year.  (4-digit years cause a lot of issues in all types if iterative fitting procedures especially if a squared year is used.)  So an additional line of code right after

might be

siteCovs$year <- siteCovs$year - 2000

Then there are no NaN's.

So this is essentially related to "standardizing" covariates.  For things like 4-digit years subtracting 2000 (or 1900 or 1990 if you're analyzing older data) is easier to do (and undo) and easier to interpret than subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation. 

Probably too much or unnecessary information:  The Hessian when using 4-digit years has two negative entries and when the inverse of that matrix is taken negative values appear along the diagonal where the estimates of variance are taken.  Taking the square root of those negative numbers results in R showing NaN's for those standard errors.

Jim

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] NaNs produced in pcount output
parts:
Just noticed your predict code.  You don't want to use exp on the predicted value.  It already is in the correct units.  So pred$Predict is what you want (and not exp(pred$Predicted)).

Jim

Thanks Jim. 

Your response is really helpful and I very much appreciate it. I had been trying to figure this out for a while, I even tried re-scaling (in line with what was suggest on a post I found somewhere). But, I just double checked my script and it seems that in the heat of the moment I was silly enough to re-scale my count data and not my predictors. Lucky there are kind people out there to help that are less silly than I am.

All the best.
